ch1Opening.text:
Welcome to the Lyte of Utopia RPG! This is a text-based game based on the web novel of the same name.

Lyte of Utopia blends cosmic fantasy with shonen-inspired battles, filled with world-shaking conflicts, layered lore, and character-driven growth. Please note that it contains **violence, gore and mature themes**

 The web novel is still ongoing, so please be patient with future updates. If you have any feedback please dm **downabyzmal** on discord. Thank you, and we hope you enjoy!

ch1Second.text:
"Move! Get out of here at once!" The shadowed man's voice cracked like thunder as he shoved a child into the pod. His hands were shaking, but his gaze burned with urgency.

The woman clutched the pod's frame, her fingers white from the grip. "No… I'm not leaving without you!" She pushed against the pod, preventing him from getting her in.

"You must," he said, his voice breaking, "our son will need you." He didn't look at her when he said it. He couldn't.

Then the ground quaked. The sound of the world breaking apart. The rest of the ships shattered like glass.

"Dammit!" He slammed the pod shut and hit the coordinates.

The hatch sealed shut with a hiss.

"Live," he whispered.

The pod shot skyward, streaking into the blackness as the world behind them collapsed into chaos.

ch1Third.text:
*At another time and place…*

"Akiraaa! Akira!?"

An old man's voice echoed through a cramped, shadowed room. A boy stirred from his sleep, face sticky with sweat. His spiky black hair was pressed firmly against his pillow.

"U-ugh." The boy rolled over groggily. "No need to be loud so early in the morning, gramps."

His black eyes slowly fought themselves open.

"I wouldn't have to be so loud if you'd woken up the first time I called you, you squirt."

The man crossed his arms at the doorway.

"Now get up, we have work to do."

ch1Fourth.text:
Pulling himself out of bed, Akira looked around the room.

It wasn't much. A single window, its shutters warped from years of weathering, let in a thin blade of morning light. A wooden chest sat against the far wall, its lid scarred where someone had once pried at it. Clothes lay folded on a stool that had seen better decades.

The sound of gulls carried in from outside. Somewhere outside gramps was already outside whistling a tune

ch1_examine_self.text:
Akira looked down at himself.

Thin. Wiry, gramps called it, which was a generous word for it. Sun-browned from working the fields. He was nothing remarkable. Nothing that would suggest he was anything other than a boy on an island at the edge of nowhere.

ch1_examine_window.text:
Through the warped glass, the land around the house and the forest beyond that greeted Akira.

It was the same view it had always been. Akira had never seen anything else.

ch1Fifth.text:
The air smelled of dew and soil. Beyond their weathered little house stretched endless golden fields under a rising sun.

Akira dragged his feet through the dirt as he walked behind the old man, squinting against the light.

"Sigh… another boring day of working in the fields with a boring old grandpa," he muttered, scratching his head.

The man didn't look back. "The sooner you stop complaining, the sooner you finish. If you have time to flap your lips, you have time to work."

Akira rolled his eyes. *Old man has always got something to say.*

ch1Sixth.text:
The two of them worked well into the evening, the heat making their ragged clothes stick to their skin.

"Okay," the old man said as he wiped the sweat from his brow, leaning against his worn hoe.

Despite his seemingly frail physique and short stature, he was a hardworking man, well into his age. The wrinkles across his face and the dry, calloused surface of his hands were proof enough.

"At this rate, we'll be ready by harvest time. I guess that means we can stop working for today." He sighed.

"Yes! Finally!"

Akira leapt into the air, arms raised like a victor as he celebrated in delight.

"Does this mean we can do some training? After we eat, of course. Definitely can't skip out on dinner," Akira said, nodding his head affirmatively.

The old man chuckled. "Sure. But first, you need to clean up these tools and wash yourself up. I need everything to be in order so that my trip to the village tomorrow can be as smooth as possible."

ch1Seventh.text:
The old man left to prepare their meal.

Akira groaned. "Fine…"

After packing away the tools, he was on his way to collect water from the well. Incidentally, he started wandering into the forest surrounding the farm.

"I still don't get why he never lets me visit the village…" he mumbled, kicking a rock down the dirt path.

The forest was alive with chirps and rustling leaves — until a low, wet tearing sound broke the peace.

Akira froze. He peeked through a thicket and saw a massive wolf hunched over a carcass, its teeth stained crimson.

*Shit.*

Even from far away, he could smell the decaying flesh. The wolf had bloody guts lodged in its teeth.

He crouched low, heart hammering against his ribs. One wrong move and—

A twig snapped.

ch1Eighth.text:
The wolf's head whipped toward him, glowing eyes locking on his position.

It was bigger standing than it had looked hunched. Shoulders level with his chest. The carcass forgotten behind it.

Akira had a bucket. No knife, no stick, nothing his hands had ever been trained to hold.

**I need to get out of here.**

ch1_wolf_death.text:
He set his feet. Raised his fists like he'd seen gramps do a hundred times in the yard.

The wolf did not care.

It crossed the distance in less time than it took him to decide he'd made a mistake, and the weight of it took him off his feet entirely. His back hit the roots. Something in his shoulder gave.

The last thing he registered was the smell — rot and iron, close enough to taste.

gameOver_wolf.text:
**You died.**

A boy from a farm on Buena Island, killed by an animal in a forest he'd walked a hundred times. No one will find him for two days. The old man will look, and keep looking, and eventually stop.

The world does not pause for this.

Somewhere far from here, a man in a red coat is still coming. He will arrive to find a house, and a basement, and an old man who has nothing left worth protecting.

It will not take him long.

ch1_wolf_bucket.text:
He threw it. The bucket caught the wolf across the snout and clattered away into the brush.

For half a second it flinched.

Then it came anyway, and now he had nothing in his hands at all.

ch1_wolf_chase.text:
Akira crawled backward, then bolted, the forest blurring as he ran.

Branches tore at his arms. He didn't feel them. Behind him the undergrowth was breaking — not running so much as *coming through*, straight, indifferent to what was in the way.

His chest burned. The trees were thinning ahead.

ch1_wolf_thicket.text:
He cut hard left into the dense brush, thorns raking his forearms.

It bought him three seconds. The wolf overshot, skidded, turned.

Three seconds was three seconds. He used them.

ch1Ninth.text:
The treeline broke.

Akira came out of the forest at a dead sprint and kept going, dirt turning to tilled soil under his feet, the golden fields opening flat and wide in every direction. He didn't stop until his legs stopped for him — twenty paces out, hands on his knees, dragging air.

He made himself turn around.

The wolf stood at the edge of the trees. Not pacing. Not circling. Just standing where the shadow ended, watching him with those pale eyes, close enough that he could still see the dark matting on its jaw.

It didn't come any further.

A long moment passed. Then it turned, unhurried, and the undergrowth closed behind it.

Akira stayed bent over in the dirt for a while after that, listening to his own breathing.

*It stopped.*

*Why did it stop?*

ch1Tenth.text:
"Are you sure I can't come?" Akira said this while the old man was loading barrels from their harvest onto a cart.

"I've already told you Akira, no, you're going to stay here and watch the house." The old man finished putting the last barrel into the cart as he said, "And that's final!"

"Aw man!" Akira whined.

The old man gave him a stern look that killed the conversation.

"That's final."

ch1_sneak_decision.text:
The cart creaked off down the path and out of sight. The house went quiet in a way it never was when gramps was in it.

An hour passed. Maybe more.

*Plenty of time has passed now. It'll still be a few hours before gramps comes back, so I should have time to check out the village and come back before him.*

The path was right there. It had always been right there.

ch1_stay_home.text:
He stayed.

He swept a floor that didn't need sweeping. He checked the tools he'd already put away. He sat on the step and watched the treeline for a while, and the treeline did nothing at all.

The sun moved maybe a finger's width.

*This is unbearable.*

ch1_stayed_home.text:
He sat back down on the step.

The sun was warm on the boards and there was nothing left to do and no one around to tell him not to. He told himself he was just resting his eyes.

He woke to the sky the wrong colour.

**Boom!**

The sound arrived a half-second after the light did — a thunderous crack that rattled the shutters and put him on his feet before he understood he was standing.

Orange. Everything to the north was orange.

*The fields—*

ch1_village_arrival.text:
Akira grinned mischievously and took off down the forest path toward the village.

The trees thinned, and then they were gone entirely, and Buena Island's village opened up in front of him.

It was *loud*. That was the first thing. Voices layered over voices, a cart rattling somewhere, someone shouting a price at someone else. Smoke that smelled like cooking instead of burning. Colour everywhere — awnings, painted shutters, cloth hung out in lines between the buildings.

Akira stood at the edge of it and forgot, briefly, that he wasn't supposed to be here.

ch1_village_hub.text:
The main street ran downhill toward the harbour, lined on both sides with stalls and open shopfronts.

A woman was frying something in oil that smelled better than anything Akira had eaten in his life. Further down, a table of trinkets caught the light. Past that, a knot of dockhands were arguing about something with more volume than seemed necessary.

And above it all, the sun. Still high. Still plenty of time.

choices.text: Head home before gramps gets back

ch1_village_food.text:
"You look like you've never seen a fried thing before," the woman said, not unkindly.

"I haven't seen *that* fried thing."

She laughed and handed him one on a stick without asking for anything. It was hot enough to hurt and he ate it anyway, standing right there, and it was — he didn't have a word for it. Gramps cooked. This was something else.

"Farm boy," she said, watching him. Not a question.

He nodded, mouth full.

"Thought so. Go on, then."

ch1_village_trinkets.text:
Carved shells. Glass beads. A knife with a handle wrapped in dyed cord that Akira picked up before he could stop himself.

"That one's not for looking," the merchant said.

He put it down.

"It's for buying." The man grinned. "Which you can't do. It's fine, kid, half the island can't. Look all you like, just don't look with your hands."

Akira looked. There was a lot to look at.

ch1_village_dockhands.text:
"—and I'm telling you it was *this* big."

"You said that last time."

"Last time it was smaller."

Three dockhands stood around a crate, one of them holding his hands apart at a width that had clearly grown since the story started.

"Barnaby. You came back with one fish."

"Because the big one *took* the others! That's the whole point of the story! You're not listening!"

"I've listened four times."

"Then you'd think you'd have it by now." He turned, spotted Akira, and pointed at him without hesitation. "You. Boy. Does that sound like a lie to you?"

Akira, who had been standing there for about nine seconds, said, "…No?"

"*Thank* you." Barnaby rounded on the others, vindicated. "The boy gets it."

"The boy would agree with a post."

"The boy has *instincts*."

ch1_village_harbour.text:
The street ended at water.

Boats knocked against the dock posts, a dozen of them, none large. Past the breakwater the sea went out flat and grey and did not stop.

Akira had seen it from his window every morning of his life. Standing at the edge of it was different. From up at the farm it looked like a view. Down here it looked like a direction.

He stayed longer than he meant to.

ch1_village_sunset.text:
The light had gone orange without him noticing.

*Oh no… the old man's gonna kill me.*

ch1_clearing.text:
"Wh-what's going on?!" he cried out.

"Grgh— get out of here! Akira!" The old man did his best to fight off the demonic beasts. "Run!"

Akira slowly approached, trying to help, but then a couple of the wolves took notice and rushed at him.

"No! Stay away from him!" The old man released his energy and attacked the wolves chasing Akira.

He knocked them back with one hit, but it wasn't enough to stop them. The wolves greatly outnumbered them seven to two.

ch1_akira_freezes.text:
"Akira, you need to get out of here, NOW!"

Hearing that sent a shock through Akira's body.

*"Get out of here at once!"*

The old man's words stirred the dreams that were deep inside Akira's mind. The shadowy figure from Akira's dreams stared him down.

Akira froze in silence, sweat slowly dripping down his cheek.

"Akira! Now!"

The wolves' eyes glowed like embers as they closed in, their low growls rumbling through the field.

"Agh!" Akira's legs locked.

He couldn't move. Couldn't breathe.

*He's going to die because of me.*

ch1_espada_santa.text:
"Akira! Run!"

The old man's voice cut through the chaos.

"Damn it…" The old man crouched low, his palms glowing with a faint golden light. "Pierce through the darkness… **Espada Santa!**"

A blade of pure light exploded from his hands, tearing through the beasts. The smell of burning flesh filled the air as the wolves howled in agony before collapsing.

Akira watched as the blood trickled out from their bodies; slowly, until they were lying motionless on the ground — pallor mortis quickly settling in.

The old man grabbed Akira by the wrist and dashed out of the field. He went straight through the woods at tremendous speeds.

ch1_felix_appears.text:
"And where do you think you're going?"

The voice was smooth, almost playful, but the aura behind it was suffocating. His demeanor was that of a predator toying with its prey.

From the tree line, a man stepped forward — tall, with spiky orange hair that caught the moonlight like fire. His smirk didn't reach his eyes, which were sharp and starved. He was wearing a flamboyant red coat with dark gray pants to match.

"You didn't even say hello."

The air grew heavy. Akira's knees wobbled, and bile rose in his throat.

*What… is this pressure?*

He felt his stomach churn. Just standing near this man made his body want to collapse.

ch1_felix_introduction.text:
"Who are you?" The old man said sternly.

"Hehehe… don't you know it's bad manners not to introduce yourself first?" He smirked as he licked his lips in a gluttonous manner.

"I won't repeat myself."

"Hmph. Fine, be that way."

His smile quickly vanished, but the deadly look in his eyes was emboldened.

"Not that it matters since I'll just kill you and take what I want. But first," he said as he took notice of Akira. "I think I'll introduce myself. I… am **Demon Lord Felix**, one of the Ten Generals of Apocalypse's Army."

"W-what! Apocalypse?!" The old man stiffened and let his guard down.

ch1_heart_of_utopia.text:
Felix waved his hand lazily.

Suddenly, like a mystical force had come over him, the old man collapsed to his knees, coughing up blood.

"Old man Haru!" Akira screamed.

"Hehehe… HAHAHA!"

Felix's laughter echoed as wolves slunk out of the shadows, circling them.

"You're through. Now give me what I want. Unless you want to die a slow and painful death."

Haru choked, spitting up blood as he glared at Felix. "I don't know what you're talking about."

"Don't play dumb with me, geezer. Where is it? Where is **The Heart of Utopia**?"

"You'll never find it…"

ch1_haru_farewell.text:
Then Haru gestured towards Akira.

"Go… get out of here," he whispered.

"No! I can't leave you!"

"You must." His voice softened. "I will stall this monster for as long as I can. But you… you need to live. Otherwise, everything I've done will have been in vain."

Haru got into his pose once again.

Akira's chest tightened. Tears blurred his vision.

"O-okay…"

ch1_ducha_sagrado.text:
Haru inhaled deeply, gathering the last of his strength.

*Yes… If this works, it will all be worth it.*

He slowly breathed out.

"Now is the time! **Ducha Sagrado!**"

A storm of golden light beams began raining down. They rampaged through the forest, destroying everything in their path — including the wolves, who trembled helplessly in their path.

However, Felix swatted them aside like gnats.

"Go now!" Haru yelled.

ch1_haru_death.text:
Akira ran as fast as he could through the forest, heading towards the nearest town to get help. He ran without looking back a single time; his own tears racing him as they fell faster than he could step.

Then he felt it — a sharp, cold shock pulsated through his body. He felt his heart squeeze like it was choked in devastation.

He didn't need to see it to know…

Haru had already been killed.

ch1_felix_basement.text:
Felix stood among the ruins, casually brushing dirt from his coat. He strolled towards Haru's home and found a trapdoor leading into the basement.

"Well now… what do we have here?" he said as he looked around.

*A Drift Sphere?! What's a space pod doing down here?*

ch1_akira_escape.text:
*Akira's Escape*

Akira didn't stop running until his legs gave out. He collapsed in the dirt, chest heaving, staring at the empty night sky.

"You said… to live." His voice cracked, barely above a whisper. "But how am I supposed to live with this?"

For the first time since Haru's death, the tears came. Akira curled into himself, fists digging into his arms as sobs wracked his body.

"I'll… I'll kill him." The words burned in his throat. "Felix… I'll make you pay."

Only when his voice broke did exhaustion pull him under, sleep taking him like a mercy.

ch1_end.text:
*End of Chapter One.*
